title: Private Deployments — Airgap-aware Upgrade Sequencing and Emergency Patch Acceptance Criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines deterministic acceptance criteria and operational requirements for performing offline (airgapped) and minimal-egress upgrades in Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to create a repeatable upgrade flow that: (1) requires at most a narrow egress allowlist or a one-time signed artifact bootstrap, (2) has automated preflight validation checks that run without outbound connectivity, and (3) includes a fast emergency patch path that can be applied with minimal operator intervention and verifiable rollback triggers.

Scope:
- Network constraints: work for closed networks where only a small set of egress endpoints may be temporarily allowed, or where operators will bring signed artifacts via mirrored registry or physical media.
- Upgrade sequencing: canary staging across operator-controlled groups, deterministic artifact verification, operator handshake protocol for offline operators.
- Emergency patches: verification, signed image promotion, zero-downtime rollback plan, and post-patch telemetry.
- Acceptance tests: both automated (CI/CD in airgapped QA) and manual runbooks for on-prem customers.

Out of scope: multi-region public cloud tooling changes and hosted API behavior.

Non-functional constraints:
- All images and manifests used in the flow must be cryptographically signed and validated by the operator before install.
- Upgrades must tolerate partial network partitioning (single-site isolation) and provide deterministic behavior when control-plane connectivity is intermittent.
- Upgrade validation must be achievable within an isolated test environment reflecting customer network topology (mirror cluster or VM-based smoke harness).
acceptance_criteria: Artifact provenance: every image and package used in upgrade path has a verifiable signature; agent verifies signatures locally using configured public key; test leverages sample signed images in the mirrored registry.

Minimal egress bootstrap: documented minimal allowlist with no more than 6 well-known endpoints (for token exchange and time sync) OR documented physical media bootstrap flow; both flows must be validated in a staged runbook.

Deterministic canary: operator can select a deterministic subset of nodes (by label) for the initial canary; canary deployment succeeds and reports health for 30 minutes before promoting; promotion steps are recorded and reversible.

Offline preflight checks: operator-run preflight script that validates disk space, KMS access (if configured), operator-agent handshake, image signatures, and network partition simulation; preflight must exit non-zero with clear remediation steps if checks fail.

Emergency patch path: an emergency patch can be packaged, signed, and applied to all nodes within a documented 2-hour window in our internal staging environment; includes automatic verification and staged rollback triggers if key metrics regress beyond threshold.

Rollback criteria: explicit metric thresholds (error rate > 1.5x baseline for 5m or 99th latency spike > 2x baseline) trigger automated rollback; rollback must succeed without requiring external egress and restore previous images and configs.

Operator handshake: offline operator can supply an operator-auth token or use a signed operator handshake file; the control plane accepts the handshake if it validates; test vectors for handshake are included in the artifacts repo.

Telemetry & observability: during staged upgrade, console shows per-route token cost, latency, and error breakdown for the canary subset; metrics must be recorded to customer telemetry sinks (or stored locally for airgapped installs) for 7 days.

KMS rotation & keys: if customer-managed KMS is in use, an upgrade flow that rotates keys must be validated end-to-end in staging with a simulated key rotation event and successful re-encryption of node secrets.
Documentation & runbooks: upgrade runbook (Confluence) and emergency patch runbook exist and have been reviewed by SOC and Field Ops; runbooks contain clear operator steps and contact points.

Validation harness: automated CI job that runs the full upgrade scenario in an airgapped emulated environment (mirrored registry + simulated network rules) and passes all smoke tests before marking release as eligible for Private deploys.
